name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project for Windows Docker, exclusively changing what is required to run it. This is .NET Framework, not .NET Core.

Settings: project `.csproj`; Windows SKU (Core default/Full); Server version (2016/2019/2022); build/run base images (“None” = standard); ports; user (default `ContainerUser`); IIS settings; pre/post-image build steps; GAC assemblies; MSIs; COM; registry; environment variables; roles/features; files and target paths; exclusions; extra `.dockerignore` patterns; health endpoint/interval/timeout; other requirements; known issues. Unspecified values use defaults.

Must include:
✅ config-builder environment settings/connection strings
✅ Dockerfile; multi-stage build/publish
✅ Windows platform compatibility
✅ dependency handling
❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed separate)
❌ No code changes beyond containerization

1. Review settings.
2. Create `progress.md`.
3. Read `TargetFrameworkVersion` from the `.csproj`.
4. Select image using framework version, SKU, and Server version. Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Ensure `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment` is installed. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If not installed, the user must install them manually; pause and ask the user to install via Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or package manager console.
6. Modify `web.config`: add `configBuilders` in `configSections` and root; configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for `appSettings` and `connectionStrings`:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
`<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">`
`<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">`
7. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` beside the Dockerfile by copying the reference. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless settings specify otherwise. Do not change EventLog logging from `Information`.
8. Create root `Dockerfile`, multi-stage:
- Build: Windows Server Core; **The build stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file**. Copy `.sln`, `.csproj`, `packages.config`, optional `NuGet.config`; configure private feeds; restore; copy source; MSBuild publish to `C:\publish`.
- Final: **The final stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file**. Copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` into (e.g.) `C:\LogMonitor`; download `LogMonitor.exe` from `https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe`; workdir `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; copy `C:\publish`; apply all settin
